sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to the Psychology of Your 20s,
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《20多岁的心理学》，

sentences.en: the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 这是一个探讨我们在20多岁时经历的一些重大生活变化与转型，以及它们对我们心理意味着什么的播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, welcome back to the podcast, new listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到本播客，无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界的哪一个角落。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要一起剖析20多岁时的心理学。

sentences.en: It has been a beautiful week for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一个美好的星期。

sentences.en: I am back from my mother-daughter trip to Fiji.
sentences.zh: 我刚结束了斐济的母女双人游，现在回来了。

sentences.en: I feel refreshed.
sentences.zh: 我感到神清气爽。

sentences.en: I feel really motivated.
sentences.zh: 我感到动力十足。

sentences.en: I feel good.
sentences.zh: 我感觉很好。

sentences.en: I literally had the best time with my mom.
sentences.zh: 我和我妈妈在一起度过了可以说是最棒的时光。

sentences.en: She is so much fun.
sentences.zh: 她实在是太有趣了。

sentences.en: So I feel like I'm back right in time to dive into work, like I had enough time away to feel excited about coming back.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得自己回来得正是时候，可以一头扎进工作中，因为我有了足够的外出时间，从而对回归充满期待。

sentences.en: And, you know, speaking of work, work is actually the subject of today's episode.
sentences.zh: 而且，说起工作，工作其实就是今天这期节目的主题。

sentences.en: Specifically, the signs that you may not be aware of or may be ignoring that your career is not right for you.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，就是那些你可能没有意识到、或者可能一直在忽视的迹象，它们表明你的职业并不适合你。

sentences.en: Not just not right for you, but deeply dissatisfying, deeply unfulfilling, deeply unrewarding.
sentences.zh: 不仅是不适合你，而且是深深地令人沮丧、深深地无法满足、深深地毫无回报。

sentences.en: And perhaps you just haven't even realized it yet.
sentences.zh: 也许你甚至还没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: These are specifically signs that I wish someone had told me when I was feeling pretty low about my previous job and I was trying so hard to make it work.
sentences.zh: 这些特定迹象是我当年对上一份工作感到非常低落、却又拼命想让它走上正轨时，多么希望有人能提醒我的。

sentences.en: And now I can acknowledge that all those things I was feeling were actually indicative that this career was just not right for me.
sentences.zh: 现在我可以承认，我当时所有的那些感受，实际上都表明这份职业根本不适合我。

sentences.en: When I look back, you know, I wish I had made a change earlier.
sentences.zh: 回首过去，你知道的，我真希望自己能早点做出改变。

sentences.en: I wish that my decision paralysis and fear of the unknown hadn't kept me in unhappy places for longer than I needed to be in them.
sentences.zh: 我真希望当时的我不会因为决策麻痹和对未知的恐惧，而在不快乐的地方停留超过必要的时间。

sentences.en: And so I'm taking some of that wisdom, some of the things that I learned,
sentences.zh: 因此，我汲取了其中的一些智慧，以及我学到的一些东西，

sentences.en: as well as some of the tips and some of the psychology to really help you guys figure out whether what you're experiencing right now is just a bad week.
sentences.zh: 还有一些技巧和心理学知识，来真正帮助大家弄清楚，你现在所经历的究竟只是糟糕的一周，

sentences.en: Or a deeper dissatisfaction with what you are doing, but more importantly, the kind of warning signs that you are becoming stagnant or stuck when you know that you are not happy.
sentences.zh: 还是对你正在做的事情有着更深层次的不满，但更重要的是，当你明知自己并不快乐时，你正在变得停滞不前或陷入困境的那些危险信号。

sentences.en: Basically,
sentences.zh: 基本上，

sentences.en: how do we make a change in our lives and have the bravery and the courage to try something new before we feel further weighed down by time and money and the education and the years that we've invested into a job or a profession that,
sentences.zh: 在我们被时间和金钱、以及投入到一份并不适合我们的工作或职业中的教育和岁月进一步拖累之前，

sentences.en: you know, simply isn't right for us.
sentences.zh: 我们该如何在生活中做出改变，并拥有尝试新事物的勇气和胆量呢？

sentences.en: So, work is really important.
sentences.zh: 所以，工作真的很重要。

sentences.en: Doing something you care about doesn't have to be aspirational, even in this current job market.
sentences.zh: 做你关心的事情并不一定非得好高骛远，即使在当前的就业市场也是如此。

sentences.en: And I want to really share how you can choose something that feels more aligned without feeling boxed in by this very notorious and incorrect idea of a dream job.
sentences.zh: 我想真正分享的是，如何在不被这种臭名昭著且不正确的“梦想工作”理念所局限的情况下，选择一种感觉更契合的方向。

sentences.en: I also want to talk about when you know it's really time to quit,
sentences.zh: 我还想谈谈，当你真正觉得是时候辞职时该怎么做，

sentences.en: even if maybe you don't have anything else lined up and also some of the surprising ways that hating your job shows up in all other dimensions of your life that you may or may not be ignoring.
sentences.zh: 即便你可能还没有找好下家，同时还要探讨讨厌工作如何在生活的其他各个维度中表现出来，而这些你可能正在忽视或尚未察觉。

sentences.en: So, if you have doubts lingering as to whether what you're doing now is really what you want to do for the rest of your life or something that you actually care about,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对你现在做的事情是否真的是你余生想做的事、或者是否是你真正关心的事情抱有挥之不去的疑虑，

sentences.en: these five signs will definitely give you some clarity and give you some of the answers that you are probably looking for.
sentences.zh: 这五个迹象绝对会给你带来一些清晰的认知，并为你可能正在寻找的答案提供线索。

sentences.en: So, without further ado, whether you're in your 20s or maybe even beyond, let's get into the signs that the career you're in right now is maybe not the one for you.
sentences.zh: 所以，闲话少说，无论你正处于20多岁还是已经过了这个年纪，让我们一起来看看那些表明你当前的职业可能并不适合你的迹象吧。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: If you have listened to the podcast for a while, you will probably know this, but it is my deep belief that when it comes to finding the right career, the right pathway,
sentences.zh: 如果你听这个播客有一段时间了，你大概会知道这一点，但我坚信，当谈到寻找合适的职业、合适的道路、

sentences.en: the right job for you, there isn't one.
sentences.zh: 适合你的合适工作时，其实并没有唯一答案。

sentences.en: There is not a perfect job.
sentences.zh: 根本没有完美的工作。

sentences.en: There is no such thing as a dream job that comes with no flaws, no downsides, no bad days, no occasional sense of emptiness.
sentences.zh: 世界上不存在那种没有瑕疵、没有缺点、没有糟糕的日子、也没有偶尔的空虚感的心仪工作。

sentences.en: And that's coming from someone who, for all intents and purposes, has the best job that they could ask for in their life right now.
sentences.zh: 这话是出自一个无论从什么角度来看，目前都拥有人生中求之不得的最好工作的人之口。

sentences.en: There are still things that I would change.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，仍然有一些事情是我想要改变的。

sentences.en: And I know that in 10, 20 years, I probably won't think the same about my job that I do now because dream jobs evolve.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道，在10年、20年后，我对工作的看法可能和现在不一样了，因为梦想的工作是会进化的。

sentences.en: Our purpose evolves.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标在演变。

sentences.en: Our idea of work-life balance is constantly being changed and being challenged.
sentences.zh: 我们对工作与生活平衡的理念也在不断地被改变和挑战。

sentences.en: That doesn't necessarily mean, though, that there isn't some careers out there that simply fit better.
sentences.zh: 但这并不一定意味着，世上就没有那些单纯更适合你的职业。

sentences.en: But I do want to give that caveat at the beginning, that if you are here to figure out what your dream job is, I'm sorry, I don't even believe in that concept.
sentences.zh: 不过在一开始，我还是想做这个免责声明：如果你来到这里是为了找出你的梦想工作是什么，很抱歉，我甚至不相信这个概念。

sentences.en: But hopefully I can bring you closer to finding a job that is maybe almost there for you.
sentences.zh: 但希望我能让你更接近找到一份对你来说差不多的工作。

sentences.en: Another thing I believe is that it's never too late to change, to shift gears, to essentially decide that you want something different.
sentences.zh: 我深信的另一件事是，改变、转换赛道、或者从根本上决定你想要不同的生活，永远都不会太晚。

sentences.en: And at the point that you realize that your major, your job, your career isn't for you, no matter how far you have gone down the wrong road, turn back.
sentences.zh: 当你意识到你的专业、你的工作、你的职业不适合你时，无论你在错误的道路上走了多远，都要回头。

sentences.en: That is a very famous Turkish proverb that I think more of us ought to live by, not just in our professional lives, but in relationships, in love, in anything.
sentences.zh: 这是一句非常著名的土耳其谚语，我认为我们更多人应该遵循它，不仅在职业生活中，在人际关系中、在爱情中、在任何事情上都应如此。

sentences.en: Careers in particular, though, you know, a lot feels at stake for a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 不过特别是职业，你知道的，由于几个原因，人们会觉得风险很大。

sentences.en: There is a couple of reasons why we know we're on the wrong path and we don't turn around.
sentences.zh: 有几个原因导致我们明知自己走错了路却依然不回头。

sentences.en: The first one being that, you know, our jobs, they allow us to live and they allow us to exist in a world that is ruled by currency and money.
sentences.zh: 第一个原因是，你知道的，我们的工作让我们得以维系生活，让我们得以在一个由货币和金钱统治的世界中生存。

sentences.en: Jobs pay our bills.
sentences.zh: 工作为我们支付账单。

sentences.en: So simply leaving without having anything else lined up.
sentences.zh: 所以要毫无退路地直接辞职。

sentences.en: I don't know about you.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你们怎么样。

sentences.en: I have never had that luxury.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有过这种奢侈的底气。

sentences.en: Secondly, you may have a lot of time, energy, resources tied up in your career.
sentences.zh: 其次，你可能在职业生涯中投入了大量的时间、精力和资源。

sentences.en: Say you're becoming a doctor or a psychologist or a tradesperson.
sentences.zh: 比如说你正在成为一名医生、心理学家或专业技术人员。

sentences.en: That typically means a lot of study, a lot of hours learning a skill, sometimes a lot of student loans, a lot of money invested.
sentences.zh: 这通常意味着大量的学习、无数小时的技能学习，有时还有大量的学生贷款和投入的大笔资金。

sentences.en: You can really feel like you're not going to get that time back.
sentences.zh: 你真的会觉得那些时间是拿不回来了。

sentences.en: You're not going to get that money back.
sentences.zh: 那些钱是拿不回来了。

sentences.en: You're letting yourself down.
sentences.zh: 你觉得自己辜负了自己。

sentences.en: You're letting your family down.
sentences.zh: 你觉得辜负了家人。

sentences.en: And that's what causes us to stay in places that we don't belong simply because of basically the sunk cost effect.
sentences.zh: 正是这种心理让我们停留在不属于我们的地方，仅仅是因为所谓的沉没成本效应。

sentences.en: We also, of course, it's not just an investment of time, energy, money.
sentences.zh: 当然，这不仅仅是时间、精力、金钱的投资。

sentences.en: It's an investment of our identity.
sentences.zh: 这也是对我们身份认同的投资。

sentences.en: What we choose to do for a living, what we hope to do for a living forms a large and significant part of who we see ourselves as.
sentences.zh: 我们选择以什么为生，我们希望以什么为生，构成了我们对自我认知的大部分和重要组成部分。

sentences.en: You know, what's one of the first things that people ask you?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，别人问你的第一件事是什么？

sentences.en: What do you do for work?
sentences.zh: 你是做什么工作的？

sentences.en: What are you studying?
sentences.zh: 你学的是什么专业？

sentences.en: It just goes to show how much occupational identity is one of the ways that we are really pigeonholed and that we pigeonhole ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰说明了职业身份认同是我们将自己归类、以及我们自我归类的重要方式之一。

sentences.en: And, you know, pigeonholes may feel very small and restrictive.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，标签可能会让人觉得非常狭隘和局限。

sentences.en: They can also feel very safe and very comfortable.
sentences.zh: 但它们也可以让人感到非常安全和舒适。

sentences.en: So deciding to walk away from whatever you're studying, whatever you're doing and explore other things, especially if you don't know what else you want to try,
sentences.zh: 因此，决定放弃你所学的专业、你正在做的事情去探索其他领域，尤其是当你不知道自己还想尝试什么时，

sentences.en: it can feel like voluntarily choosing to step off a ledge into a large bottomless pit.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就像是自愿选择从悬崖边迈出一步，跳入一个巨大的无底深渊。

sentences.en: But being in the wrong place, it doesn't get easier.
sentences.zh: 但身处错误的地方并不会变得更容易。

sentences.en: Your tolerance for it just improves until, you know, one day you're in your 60s and you're looking back at your life and you're realizing how truly young you were,
sentences.zh: 你对它的忍耐力只是在不断提高，直到有一天，当你60岁回首往事时，你才会意识到自己当时是多么的年轻，

sentences.en: how much time you actually really did have ahead of you if you'd just taken the risk and walked away a little bit sooner from the thing that you knew deep down you didn't love.
sentences.zh: 如果你当初能冒着风险早点离开那个内心深处明知并不喜欢的事情，你的前方其实还有大把的时间。

sentences.en: So to avoid that regret, to give ourselves that opportunity, let's discuss these five signs that you are probably in the wrong career.
sentences.zh: 所以为了避免那种遗憾，为了给我们自己创造那样的机会，让我们来讨论这五个迹象，它们表明你可能正处于错误的职业中。

sentences.en: Sign one, you feel emotionally numb.
sentences.zh: 迹象一，你感到情感麻木。

sentences.en: You dread what you're doing and it's a feeling that goes way beyond boredom.
sentences.zh: 你对你正在做的事情感到恐惧，这种感觉远远超出了无聊的范畴。

sentences.en: If you dread every Monday, you feel your mood completely shift the moment you walk into work, you completely detach, you don't care if you're fired,
sentences.zh: 如果你对每个星期一都感到恐惧，一走进公司就感觉情绪彻底转变，你完全抽离了出去，哪怕被解雇也无所谓，

sentences.en: you don't care if your work is good, you don't care if the assignment is late, you just have no desire to commit or succeed in what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 你不在乎工作做的好坏，不在乎任务是否延期，你对正在做的事情完全失去了投入或成功的渴望。

sentences.en: This is probably the wrong career for you.
sentences.zh: 这大概率是一份不适合你的职业。

sentences.en: Yes, a job isn't always going to put a fire in your belly every single day, but if this is what you're going to spend the large majority of your life doing,
sentences.zh: 没错，工作不可能每天都让你充满激情，但如果这是你要度过你人生绝大部分时间的事情，

sentences.en: almost 90,000 hours of your life, according to some estimates, you want to feel something.
sentences.zh: 根据一些估计，这几乎是你人生中的9万个小时，你总得去感受点什么吧。

sentences.en: Pride, accomplishment, that you're helping people, whatever it is, even on hard days, you want to feel something.
sentences.zh: 自豪感、成就感、你在帮助别人，无论是什么，哪怕是在艰难的日子里，你也希望有所感触。

sentences.en: You don't want to feel nothing and you most certainly don't want to feel just plain anxiety.
sentences.zh: 你不想什么都感觉不到，你当然更不想只感受到纯粹的焦虑。

sentences.en: The Sunday scaries are another indicator of this.
sentences.zh: 周日恐惧症就是这一现象的另一个表现。

sentences.en: Sunday scaries, it's a common term, you've most likely heard of it, but if not,
sentences.zh: 周日恐惧症，这是一个很常见的词，你大概率听说过，但如果没有的话，

sentences.en: it essentially refers to the anxiety or dread that many people experience on a Sunday evening as the weekend ends and the work week begins and it has a scientific explanation.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是指许多人在周日晚上随着周末结束、工作周开始时所体验到的焦虑或恐惧，这其实有着科学的解释。

sentences.en: Sunday scaries, it's essentially emotional forecasting or anticipatory dread.
sentences.zh: 周日恐惧症，本质上就是情感预测或预期性恐惧。

sentences.en: You're looking at the week ahead and almost feeling empathy for your future self and what you'll know they have to endure and kind of almost borrowing their unhappiness so that you feel terrible right now.
sentences.zh: 你看着接下来的这一周，几乎是在为未来的自己以及你知道他们将要忍受的痛苦感到同情，并且几乎是提前借支了他们的不快乐，好让自己现在就感觉糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And the more you experience this and endure this, the more you start to become quite numb.
sentences.zh: 你经历和忍受这种状况越多，你就越开始变得相当麻木。

sentences.en: Once you get into work or back to school or to your internship or whatever, instead of feeling all that anxiety you were feeling on Sunday, you actually end up shutting off.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始上班、回学校、去实习或做别的什么，你非但没有释放周日感受到的所有焦虑，反而最终彻底关闭了情感开关。

sentences.en: You go through the motions.
sentences.zh: 你只是在例行公事。

sentences.en: All of this is a way to kind of mentally compartmentalize rather than really acknowledging like, wow, I really hate this.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切其实是一种在精神上进行自我区隔的方式，而不是真正去承认：“哇，我是真的很讨厌这个。”

sentences.en: Because realizing that you really hate this means that you probably have to do something about it and you just might not feel ready for that.
sentences.zh: 因为意识到自己真的很讨厌这份工作，意味着你可能不得不采取行动，而你可能还没做好准备。

sentences.en: So this can also be highly indicative of something else called emotional blunting, where you basically become numb to what is going on around you.
sentences.zh: 因此，这也非常强烈地暗示了另一种被称为情感钝化的现象，在这种状态下，你基本上对周围发生的事情变得麻木了。

sentences.en: It's typically associated with certain medications such as antidepressants,
sentences.zh: 它通常与某些药物（如抗抑郁药）有关，

sentences.en: but it can also have an environmental origin like a workplace or a job that you really hate or you feel absolutely nothing positive towards.
sentences.zh: 但它也可能源于环境因素，比如你真的很讨厌、或者对它完全产生不出任何积极感受的工作场所或工作。

sentences.en: Now, if this gets worse, this can also develop into something that psychologists call anhedonia.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果这种情况恶化，它甚至可能发展成心理学家所称的快感缺乏。

sentences.en: So a lack of interest, a lack of enjoyment, a lack of pleasure in what you're experiencing.
sentences.zh: 也就是对你所经历的一切缺乏兴趣、缺乏享受、缺乏快乐。

sentences.en: Almost like people describe it like looking at your life and feeling like there is a tinge of gray over everything.
sentences.zh: 人们常常形容它就像是审视自己的生活，感觉每样东西上面都笼罩着一层灰蒙蒙的色彩。

sentences.en: And in this context, the context of our jobs and our careers, it often stems from being in an environment where your core values and your interests are being forced to be put away.
sentences.zh: 在这种语境下——也就是我们的工作和职业语境下，它通常源于身处这样一个环境：你的核心价值观和兴趣被迫收起。

sentences.en: And you may not even realize how emotionally flat you've become until the weekend or until you're on holiday or until you're working on a side project and suddenly you come alive again.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能没有意识到自己变得多么情感麻木，直到周末到来、或者你在度假、或者你在做一个副业时，你突然又活了过来。

sentences.en: It's like this is where you really feel like yourself.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉就像是，这才是你真正觉得像自己的时刻。

sentences.en: This kind of chronic disconnection throughout the work week or whenever you're studying or whenever you're engaged in the thing that isn't right for you.
sentences.zh: 这种长期的抽离感会贯穿整个工作周，或者每当你学习时，或者每当你从事那件并不适合你的事情时。

sentences.en: So this is your mind and your body communicating and essentially saying, this is this is not fitting the bill for what makes us happy.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是你的心灵和大脑在向你沟通，本质上是在说：“这并不符合我们快乐的标准。”

sentences.en: And because we can't acknowledge how unhappy we are, we're not going to feel anything.
sentences.zh: 正因为我们无法承认自己有多么不快乐，所以我们干脆什么感觉都没有了。

sentences.en: This is intrinsically linked to the second sign that you are in the wrong career, which is that your identity and what you are doing for work feel entirely out of sync.
sentences.zh: 这与你身处错误职业的第二个迹象有着内在的联系，那就是你的个人认同感与你的工作内容完全不合拍。

sentences.en: A 2016 study from the Journal of Vocational Behavior, it essentially found that career satisfaction is incredibly linked to something called identity alignment.
sentences.zh: 《职业行为杂志》2016年的一项研究发现，职业满意度与一种名为“认同一致性”的概念紧密相连。

sentences.en: How much your job reflects who you are, the more identity alignment you have, the happier you are going to be doing what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 你的工作越能反映你是谁，你的认同一致性就越高，你从事这项工作时就会越快乐。

sentences.en: There was a poll a couple of years ago, maybe even like a decade ago, that found almost 55% of Americans derive a really large part of their identity from their job.
sentences.zh: 几年前甚至大约十年前曾有过一项民意调查，发现近55%的美国人将他们身份认同的很大一部分归功于自己的工作。

sentences.en: And I think as our time spent in the office and working increases significantly year by year, I can only imagine that that identity investment has really increased.
sentences.zh: 我想，随着我们在办公室和工作上花费的时间年复一年地显著增加，我可以想象这种对身份的投资确实也随之增加了。

sentences.en: If you value helping others and your job is denying insurance claims, you will experience deep cognitive dissonance because you don't have identity alignment.
sentences.zh: 如果你珍视帮助他人，而你的工作却是拒绝保险理赔，你就会经历深刻的认知失调，因为你缺乏认同一致性。

sentences.en: If you love nature and you love being outdoors and you work a desk job with no windows, same issue.
sentences.zh: 如果你热爱大自然，喜欢待在户外，却做着一份连窗户都没有的办公室工作，也会面临同样的问题。

sentences.en: If you really value intellectualism and being cognitively stimulated, but you work a job that is very routine and process-based with not much room for creativity, again,
sentences.zh: 如果你非常看重知识性以及认知上的刺激，但你做的是一份非常常规、基于流程且几乎没有创造空间的工作，同样也是如此，

sentences.en: you have a disalignment.
sentences.zh: 你出现了不契合的状态。

sentences.en: A disalignment in your identity is the same as a disalignment in your body.
sentences.zh: 你身份的不契合，就如同你身体的不契合一样。

sentences.en: It feels pretty terrible and you can tell that something is wrong.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉非常糟糕，而且你能感觉到有什么不对劲。

sentences.en: This is very similar to a concept called self-concept clarity.
sentences.zh: 这非常类似于一个叫做自我概念清晰度的概念。

sentences.en: So self-concept clarity is basically our ability to tell what's going to make us happy and our ability to know what would make us satisfied.
sentences.zh: 所以自我概念清晰度基本上就是我们分辨什么能让我们快乐的能力，以及我们知道什么能让我们满足的能力。

sentences.en: So if you find yourself saying things like, this just really doesn't feel like me, like I hate who this makes me, I don't recognize who I am at work, I feel like someone else,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你发现自己说出这样的话：“这真的一点都不像我”、“我讨厌这让我变成了什么样的人”、“我在工作中都快认不出自己了”、“我觉得自己像个别人”，

sentences.en: that's not trivial.
sentences.zh: 这可不是小事。

sentences.en: That is indicative that your self-concept clarity is coming into play and is communicating with you and telling you like, this isn't who we are, this isn't who we want to be.
sentences.zh: 这表明你的自我概念清晰度正在发挥作用，并在与你交流，告诉你：“这不是我们是谁，这不是我们想成为的人。”

sentences.en: If you're not living your life in line with who you think you are, you know, who are you then?
sentences.zh: 如果你过着的生活与你认为的自己不一致，你知道，那你是谁呢？

sentences.en: Like if our life and the kind of person we are is defined by our actions and our actions and our time and where we work and all these other things is saying the opposite and representing the opposite of who we are,
sentences.zh: 就像如果我们的人生以及我们是怎样的人是由我们的行动所定义的，而我们的行动、我们的时间、我们工作的地方以及所有这些其他事情却在说着相反的话，代表着我们本色的对立面，

sentences.en: we are going to be very unhappy in your body and the rest of your sense of self will respond to that.
sentences.zh: 我们在自己的身体里就会非常不快乐，而你的其余自我意识也会对此作出反应。

sentences.en: We know through research that this dissatisfaction becomes very tangible.
sentences.zh: 通过研究我们知道，这种不满会变得非常切实。

sentences.en: It becomes very felt in your body, in your mind, in your bones, in your muscles.
sentences.zh: 它会在你的身体里、你的脑海里、你的骨子里、你的肌肉里被真切地感受到。

sentences.en: In order to discover what the alternative would be, you know, what would actually make us happier?
sentences.zh: 为了找出替代方案会是什么，你知道的，究竟什么才能让我们更快乐？

sentences.en: What would my so-called dream job be that isn't this?
sentences.zh: 我所谓的不是现在这样的梦想工作会是什么？

sentences.en: We really need to then focus on values because if we're living or having a career that is creating disalignment,
sentences.zh: 那么我们真的需要把重点放在价值观上，因为如果我们过着的生活或从事的职业正在产生不契合，

sentences.en: the only way to bring back alignment is to really, really reaffirm what we care about and then find ways to seek that out through work.
sentences.zh: 找回契合的唯一方法就是真正地、反复地重申我们在乎的是什么，然后通过工作去寻找这些东西。

sentences.en: This question that someone asked me once, I think, is a really great way to do that.
sentences.zh: 有人曾经问过我这个问题，我认为这是做到这一点的绝佳方法。

sentences.en: If you're struggling with what you really want to do in your life, you just know it's not this.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在纠结自己究竟想在生活中做些什么，你只知道绝不是现在这样。

sentences.en: I think this question will help.
sentences.zh: 我想这个问题会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Basically, if your whole identity, all your memories, everything about your life had been erased, about who you were as a person had been erased,
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你的整个身份、你所有的记忆、关于你生活的一切、关于你作为一个人是谁都被抹去了，

sentences.en: what are the five values that you have right now that you would choose to come back first?
sentences.zh: 你现在拥有的哪五种价值观是你愿意选择首先恢复的？

sentences.en: It's basically a different way of asking, who do you see yourself as, like at your core?
sentences.zh: 这基本上是换一种方式在问：你如何看待自己，比如在你的核心深处？

sentences.en: What are the five things that you think represent you the most?
sentences.zh: 你认为哪五件事最能代表你？

sentences.en: And is it that far-fetched that you can't ask for your work to reflect that?
sentences.zh: 要求你的工作反映这一点，难道真的有那么遥不可及吗？

sentences.en: If that feels like a stretch from where you are now, if those five things are not reflected in your work at all,
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得从你现在的处境来看这有点勉强，如果这五件事在你的工作中根本没有体现，

sentences.en: imagine then going forward and living another 30, 40 years where your values aren't aligned.
sentences.zh: 那么想象一下，接下来再去过30年、40年价值观不一致的生活会怎样。

sentences.en: The reason I think this exercise works so well for people who are unsure of what they want to do is it's not asking you to identify your dream job as an alternative.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个练习对那些不确定自己想做什么的人之所以如此有效，是因为它并没有要求你把梦想工作当作替代方案来确定。

sentences.en: Like I was having this discussion with my friend on a walk this morning and she was like, I don't know what my dream job is.
sentences.zh: 就像今天早上散步时我和朋友讨论这个话题，她说：“我不知道我的梦想工作是什么。”

sentences.en: And I was like, well, you probably don't have one.
sentences.zh: 然后我说：“嗯，你可能根本没有。”

sentences.en: You probably will never figure out what it is.
sentences.zh: 你可能永远也搞不清楚它到底是什么。

sentences.en: If you search for that your entire life, you'll probably be unhappy.
sentences.zh: 如果你一生都在寻找那个，你大概会很不快乐。

sentences.en: But what you can do is figure out a kind of broad range of things that you would feel really fulfilled doing.
sentences.zh: 但你能做到的是，找出大致范围的一类事情，让你做起来会感到真正的充实。

sentences.en: You know, and that's what this allows you to do.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是这个练习能让你做到的。

sentences.en: It's asking you to identify your values, which can then be expressed in different ways through different careers, not just one thing.
sentences.zh: 它要求你确定自己的价值观，然后这些价值观可以通过不同的职业以不同的方式表达出来，而不单单是一件工作。

sentences.en: For example, if one of the values that you would want back is, let's say, vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你想找回的价值观之一是，比方说，脆弱感。

sentences.en: Vulnerability as a core value could mean that you could be a counselor.
sentences.zh: 脆弱感作为核心价值观意味着你可以成为一名心理咨询师。

sentences.en: You could also be a matchmaker.
sentences.zh: 你也可以成为一名红娘。

sentences.en: You could be a hospice nurse.
sentences.zh: 你可以成为一名临终关怀护士。

sentences.en: You could be a rehab director.
sentences.zh: 你可以成为一名康复中心主任。

sentences.en: Many options, not one dream job, but all rooted in what you value.
sentences.zh: 有很多选择，不是只有一个梦想工作，但都根植于你所珍视的价值。

sentences.en: It's really, really important that you have that in your work.
sentences.zh: 在你的工作中拥有这一点真的、真的很重要。

sentences.en: It's worth mentioning as well what happens when we derive too much identity from work.
sentences.zh: 同样值得一提的是，当我们从工作中汲取过多的身份认同合集时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Because that can really result in something equally kind of scary.
sentences.zh: 因为这确实会导致某种同样有点可怕的结果。

sentences.en: It's called enmeshment, where you and your job are just never separate.
sentences.zh: 这叫做共生纠缠，也就是你和你的工作永远无法分离。

sentences.en: Your success at work determines your worth everywhere else.
sentences.zh: 你在工作中的成功决定了你在其他地方的价值。

sentences.en: Your interests, all work.
sentences.zh: 你的兴趣，全都是工作。

sentences.en: You can hear people getting sick of you talking about work.
sentences.zh: 你能听到人们厌烦你谈论工作。

sentences.en: Everything you think about, work.
sentences.zh: 你脑子里想的一切，全都是工作。

sentences.en: Like, I will admit, I fell into this trap when I first started doing my podcast full-time.
sentences.zh: 比如，我承认，当我刚开始全职做播客时，我也陷入了这个陷阱。

sentences.en: And then mantra as well.
sentences.zh: 还有 Mantra 也是。

sentences.en: You know, I love both of those podcasts so much.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我太喜欢这两档播客了。

sentences.en: And it was, they are such a reflection of who I am.
sentences.zh: 它们太能反映我是谁了。

sentences.en: And so much time goes into making them good and successful.
sentences.zh: 为了让它们变得优质和成功，投入了大量的时间。

sentences.en: And when I first started, there was so much at stake.
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始的时候，赌注太大了。

sentences.en: Like, I'd quit my full-time job.
sentences.zh: 比如，我辞掉了全职工作。

sentences.en: Like, there wasn't much room for me to think about anything else.
sentences.zh: 比如，我几乎没有余力去思考别的事情。

sentences.en: And also because this podcast, the one you're listening to, like, this used to be a hobby, right?
sentences.zh: 而且也因为这个播客，也就是你正在听的这个，以前是个爱好，对吧？

sentences.en: And then, like, this was the place I went to kind of not think about work.
sentences.zh: 然后，这就成了我去不去想工作的地方。

sentences.en: And then suddenly it was my job.
sentences.zh: 结果突然间它成了我的工作。

sentences.en: And nothing filled its place.
sentences.zh: 而且没有什么能填补它的空缺。

sentences.en: Like, I didn't have any sense of balance in my life.
sentences.zh: 比如，我的生活中没有任何平衡感可言。

sentences.en: My entire identity was this.
sentences.zh: 我的整个身份就是这个。

sentences.en: And, oh my gosh, was I completely uninteresting.
sentences.zh: 而且，天哪，我是多么的索然无味。

sentences.en: Especially to myself.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对我自己而言。

sentences.en: Like, I was bored of myself.
sentences.zh: 比如，我都对自己感到厌烦了。

sentences.en: I was exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: All the small setbacks felt enormous.
sentences.zh: 所有的微小挫折都感觉像是天大的事。

sentences.en: Because there was so much being balanced on the back of my career.
sentences.zh: 因为有太多东西都在我的职业生涯这块背脊上平衡着。

sentences.en: So, you can take it too far.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能会做得过头。

sentences.en: I think it's our reminder as well to, it's okay to want to be your values to be reflected in work.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是在提醒我们：希望自己的价值观在工作中得到体现，这是可以的。

sentences.en: But you also have to be bigger than work.
sentences.zh: 但你也必须比工作更伟大。

sentences.en: Me and my boyfriend have this rule.
sentences.zh: 我和男友有个规矩。

sentences.en: Before we talk about work when we get home, we have to talk about something else.
sentences.zh: 我们到家后，在谈论工作之前，必须先聊点别的。

sentences.en: It's a podcast, the gym, a story we heard, something, like, we're excited about, something in the news.
sentences.zh: 比如某个播客、健身房、听来的故事、什么让我们兴奋的事，或者新闻里的某条内容。

sentences.en: It's really important for us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说真的很重要。

sentences.en: Because both of us are deeply invested in what we do for a living.
sentences.zh: 因为我们俩都全身心投入在我们的谋生职业中。

sentences.en: I like to visualize it as a five-finger test for whether you have balance.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把它形象化为一个“五指测试”，用来检验你是否拥有平衡。

sentences.en: If you hold up five fingers, if work is one of your fingers, you have to have four things to fill the other fingers.
sentences.zh: 如果你伸出五根手指，如果工作是你的其中一根手指，你必须有另外四样东西来填满其他手指。

sentences.en: You have to have a hobby.
sentences.zh: 你必须有一个爱好。

sentences.en: You have to have an intereSt.
sentences.zh: 你必须有一个兴趣。

sentences.en: You have to have friends.
sentences.zh: 你必须有朋友。

sentences.en: Friends, you have to have four other things that you really care about.
sentences.zh: 朋友，你必须有另外四件你真正关心的事情。

sentences.en: And if you cannot assign each of your fingers something else in your life that feels as important as work,
sentences.zh: 如果你无法为你的每一根手指指定生活中其他感觉和工作一样重要的事情，

sentences.en: like, that is a warning and that is a sign to rethink where your energy is being directed to.
sentences.zh: 那么，这就是一个警告，也是一个信号，提醒你重新思考你的精力正被导向何方。

sentences.en: Like, your identity is a series of buckets.
sentences.zh: 比如，你的身份是一系列的水桶。

sentences.en: Work is just one bucket.
sentences.zh: 工作只是其中一个水桶。

sentences.en: We want to have other things that we value and other things that we care about.
sentences.zh: 我们希望拥有其他我们珍视的事物以及其他我们在乎的事物。

sentences.en: Like, literally do it right now.
sentences.zh: 比如，现在就照做。

sentences.en: Hold up five fingers.
sentences.zh: 伸出五根手指。

sentences.en: If work is one, what are the others?
sentences.zh: 如果工作是其中一个，其他的是什么？

sentences.en: What else might you need in your life to feel like your identity is reflected in what you do, but it's not everything?
sentences.zh: 你的生活中可能还需要什么，才能让你觉得自己的身份体现在你所做的事情中，但又并非全部？

sentences.en: So those are our first two signs.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是我们的前两个信号。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break here, but when we return, I have three final indicators that maybe what you're doing right now is not exactly right for you.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里稍作休息，但当我们回来时，我将带来最后三个指标，表明你现在做的事情可能并不完全适合你。

sentences.en: So stay with us.

sentences.zh: 通往更多可能的道路从这里开始，宝马展车特卖会现正火热进行中，一直持续到11月15日。

sentences.zh: 须遵守相关条款与条件。

sentences.en: Some items we hold on to because they take us straight back to a moment.
sentences.zh: 有些物件我们一直留着，因为它们能瞬间把我们带回某一个时刻。

sentences.en: A photo, a piece of clothing, a tiny souvenir from somewhere unforgettable.
sentences.zh: 一张照片、一件衣服、某个难忘地方的小纪念品。

sentences.en: In my new podcast, Charmed, with Sam Todd, we explore the memories, obsessions, and personal treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: 在我的新播客《Charmed, with Sam Todd》中，我们探索了那些成为我们生命一部分的记忆、执念和个人珍宝。

sentences.en: From the sublime all the way to the absolutely ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 从高雅脱俗一直到荒谬绝伦。

sentences.en: It's a fascinating deep dive into the keepsakes we hold close and the memories that make them special.
sentences.zh: 这是一次引人入胜的深度探究，聚焦于我们珍藏的纪念物以及赋予它们特殊意义的回忆。

sentences.en: Charmed with me, Sam Todd.
sentences.zh: 被我迷住了吗，萨姆·托德。

sentences.zh: OMF 的黑色星期五促销现已开启。

sentences.zh: 一年只有一次，所以下手要快。

sentences.en: I've been really trying to prioritize my health in a realistic way this year, and something that has kept me really motivated is my whoop.
sentences.zh: 今年我一直在努力以一种切合实际的方式将健康放在首位，而有一件让我保持极高动力的事情就是我的 Whoop 手环。

sentences.en: I am such a data person, which is why I love whoop, because I can genuinely see why my body feels differently depending on the day, why I'm running differently,
sentences.zh: 我是一个彻头彻尾的数据控，这就是为什么我喜欢 Whoop，因为我能真切地看出为什么我的身体在不同日子里会有不同的感觉，为什么我跑步的状态不一样，

sentences.en: why I'm maybe less focused.
sentences.zh: 为什么我可能注意力不太集中。

sentences.en: Whoop effortlessly tracks my sleep, it tracks my strain, my recovery, my stress, and most importantly, my overall health.
sentences.zh: Whoop 能够轻松追踪我的睡眠、追踪我的身体负荷、恢复情况、压力水平，最重要的是，我的整体健康状况。

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它只是把所有这些数据和模式提供给我，以便我能做出更好的决定，其中包括知道什么时候该轻松一点，什么时候该加把劲。

sentences.en: New members can try whoop with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新会员在承诺加入会员之前，可以先通过 30 天免费试用来体验 Whoop。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of whoop.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com/psychology 即可免费体验一个月的 Whoop。

sentences.en: Okay, are you ready for the third sign that your career is not right for you?
sentences.zh: 好了，你准备好迎接第三个信号了吗？证明你的职业不适合你。

sentences.en: Here it is.
sentences.zh: 就是这个。

sentences.en: You think more about your quitting story than your five-year plan in this career, in this company, in this industry.
sentences.zh: 在这个职业、这家公司、这个行业里，你对离职故事的想象，要多于对五年规划的构想。

sentences.en: Everyone loves a good quitting story.
sentences.zh: 每个人都喜欢听精彩的离职故事。

sentences.en: I remember when I worked at a steak restaurant back in uni, it was so horrific.
sentences.zh: 我记得还在读大学时我在一家牛排餐厅工作，那简直太可怕了。

sentences.en: Every single day, I would walk in to the start of my shift and I think, this is the day I'm going to do it.
sentences.zh: 每天一进门开始上班，我就会想：“今天就是我要付诸行动的日子。”

sentences.en: Like, I just need one reason to push me over the edge and I will quit.
sentences.zh: 比如，我只需要一个理由把我推向边缘，然后我就会辞职。

sentences.en: I will do it.
sentences.zh: 我会说到做到。

sentences.en: Knowing that I wouldn't because I needed the job.
sentences.zh: 明知自己不会这么做，因为我需要这份工作。

sentences.en: And then, you know, COVID came along and stole my epic quitting story for me.
sentences.zh: 然后呢，新冠疫情来了，把我的史诗级离职故事给偷走了。

sentences.en: But the fact that I was thinking about quitting constantly at work indicated a much deeper unhappiness.
sentences.zh: 但我在工作中不断想着离职这一事实，表明了一种更深层次的不快乐。

sentences.en: Quitting for you, it may be becoming a fixation.
sentences.zh: 对你来说，离职可能正在变成一种执念。

sentences.en: An obsessive interest that you cannot stop circling and that won't stop dominating the new cycle of your brain.
sentences.zh: 一种让你欲罢不能、在脑海中反复盘旋且占据你思维循环的强迫性兴趣。

sentences.en: You fantasize about burning your life to the ground, crashing out, disappearing, just not coming in one day, moving to Costa Rica, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 你幻想把自己的生活付之一炬、彻底摆烂、人间蒸发、某天突然就不来上班了、搬去哥斯达黎加，无论那是什么。

sentences.en: That is all you can think about.
sentences.zh: 那是你满脑子只想的事情。

sentences.en: It brings you joy to think about it.
sentences.zh: 光是想想这事就带给你快乐。

sentences.en: Being invested in the fantasy more than reality is indicative that this isn't right for you.
sentences.zh: 比起现实，你更沉迷于幻想，这表明这并不适合你。

sentences.en: You know, daydreaming, it isn't always bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道，白日做梦并不总是坏事。

sentences.en: It can actually be a really creative coping mechanism.
sentences.zh: 它实际上可以成为一种非常具有创造力的应对机制。

sentences.en: But if you're constantly escaping into the idea of doing something else, being someone else professionally, that's not just your imagination.
sentences.zh: 但如果你总是逃避到做别的事情、在职业上成为别人的想法中，那可不仅仅是你的想象力。

sentences.en: That is cognitive separation.
sentences.zh: 那是认知上的分离。

sentences.en: That is escapism at work.
sentences.zh: 那是工作中的逃避现实。

sentences.en: It has another name as well, maladaptive daydreaming.
sentences.zh: 它还有另一个名字，叫做适应不良性白日梦。

sentences.en: If you've listened to the whole episode that we did on this, you will know what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 如果你听过我们关于这个主题的完整单集，你就会知道我在说什么。

sentences.en: But maladaptive daydreaming is essentially where you feel detached from reality because you're spending too much time in the fantasy of what could be.
sentences.zh: 但适应不良性白日梦本质上是指：你感觉自己脱离了现实，因为你花了太多时间沉浸在可能发生之事的幻想中。

sentences.en: And it does mean that you end up neglecting real life responsibilities, real life relationships, work relationships, deadlines, all those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 这确实意味着你最终会忽视现实生活中的责任、现实生活中的人际关系、工作关系、截止日期以及所有这类事情。

sentences.en: In those instances where you're obsessing over the idea of quitting, I'm going to be completely honest with you.
sentences.zh: 在那些你对离职的想法着迷不已的情况下，我要对你完全坦诚。

sentences.en: It's probably not going to get better.
sentences.zh: 这种情况可能不会好转了。

sentences.en: It's probably time to start searching for a better job.
sentences.zh: 也许是时候开始寻找一份更好的工作了。

sentences.en: It's like what they say about a relationship, right?
sentences.zh: 这就跟他们对恋爱关系的说法一样，对吧？

sentences.en: Once you have seriously considered breaking up or once you have gotten the ick over somebody, you're not going back from that.
sentences.zh: 一旦你认真考虑过分手，或者一旦你对某人生出厌恶之情，你就再也回不去了。

sentences.en: No matter how long you hold on for afterwards, once you have seriously quit a relationship or quit a job in your mind, it's never going to be the same.
sentences.zh: 不管你之后坚持了多久，一旦你在心里真正决定放弃一段感情或一份工作，一切就再也回不去了。

sentences.en: It might not be quitting your imagining as well, like it might be something else, like fantasizing about a different job, fantasizing about your next holiday,
sentences.zh: 这可能不仅仅是放弃你的想象，比如它可能是别的东西，比如幻想一份不同的工作，幻想你的下一个假期，

sentences.en: the next time you switch off.
sentences.zh: 下一次你走神的时候。

sentences.en: That's going to become unhealthy and it can actually end up, you know, you can end up sabotaging your current career and sabotaging where you're currently at.
sentences.zh: 那将变得很不健康，而且它实际上最终会——你知道的——你最终可能会破坏你目前的职业生涯，破坏你目前的处境。

sentences.en: The thing is, as much as you hate your job right now, you do want to get another one.
sentences.zh: 问题是，尽管你现在多么讨厌你的工作，你确实还是想再找一份。

sentences.en: And that means having good references and having positive working relationships.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要有好的推荐信和积极的工作关系。

sentences.en: It is something I wish I had learned earlier in my 20s.
sentences.zh: 这是我希望在二十多岁时早点学会的事情。

sentences.en: Don't burn bridges based on momentary feelings.
sentences.zh: 不要因为一时冲动而过河拆桥。

sentences.en: You never know when you'll need that bridge later on.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道以后什么时候会需要那座桥。

sentences.en: So instead, try and keep at least one foot in your day to day and maybe participate in a little bit of quiet quitting.
sentences.zh: 所以相反，试着至少把一只脚留在日常生活中，也许参与一点悄悄离职。

sentences.en: But think about the future here.
sentences.zh: 但要为这里的美好未来着想。

sentences.en: Don't just completely, like, neglect your job.
sentences.zh: 不要只是完全、像那样忽视你的工作。

sentences.en: Think about it smart.
sentences.zh: 要聪明地思考。

sentences.en: And don't, please don't, just let yourself think that this is how everyone feels about work.
sentences.zh: 而且不要，请千万不要，让自己觉得这就是所有人对工作的感受。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 根本不是。

sentences.en: You don't have to feel this way.
sentences.zh: 你没必要有这种感觉。

sentences.en: You know, the best part of your day should not be the 30 minutes at lunch where you fantasize about how nice it would be to never go back in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你一天中最美好的时光不应该是午休的30分钟，当时你还在幻想不用再回去上班有多好。

sentences.en: You're allowed to want more.
sentences.zh: 你有权力想要更多。

sentences.en: You are allowed to seek more for yourself.
sentences.zh: 你有权力为自己寻求更多。

sentences.en: So use this fantasy as motivation so that you don't find yourself stagnant.
sentences.zh: 所以把这种幻想当作动力，这样你就不会发现自己停滞不前。

sentences.en: You don't find yourself thinking, well, everyone feels this way.
sentences.zh: 你不会发现自己觉得，好吧，所有人都是这么想的。

sentences.en: Like, I'll just put up with it.
sentences.zh: 就像，我只能忍着。

sentences.en: Speaking of everyone, here is the fourth sign.
sentences.zh: 说到所有人，这里是第四个迹象。

sentences.en: And I rarely hear people talk about this when it comes to knowing a career isn't right for you.
sentences.zh: 当谈到如何知道一个职业是否不适合你时，我很少听到人们谈论这一点。

sentences.en: Quite simply, if there is no one that you admire in your industry, this industry is not right for you.
sentences.zh: 很简单，如果你的行业里没有一个你崇拜的人，这个行业就不适合你。

sentences.en: No role model, no colleagues you want to be, no person, you know, 10 years down the line whose life you think looks really great,
sentences.zh: 没有榜样，没有你想成为的同事，没有那种你知道的、十年后你觉得生活看起来非常棒的人，

sentences.en: no vision of a life you want that contains your job, no examples of it.
sentences.zh: 没有包含你这份工作的美好生活愿景，没有任何这样的例子。

sentences.en: Not having this admiration is often indicative of not having aspiration or inspiration for what you're doing, essentially meaning that your heart isn't in it.
sentences.zh: 缺乏这种崇拜往往表明你对你所做的事情缺乏渴望或灵感，本质上意味着你的心不在焉。

sentences.en: It also means you probably don't see yourself here long term enough to think aspirationally about what your life could become and to seek out those examples as blueprints and motivators because you are motivated.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着你可能没有把长远的眼光放在这里，无法对你未来的生活抱有渴望，也无法去寻找那些作为蓝图和动力的例子，因为你是有动力的。

sentences.en: When you think about a good life, when you think about a life that you want for yourself, those dreams might not contain this career.
sentences.zh: 当你想象美好的生活，当你想象你为自己向往的生活时，那些梦想可能并不包含这份职业。

sentences.en: What is that saying to you?
sentences.zh: 这说明了什么？

sentences.en: Our brains are naturally drawn to admiration and sometimes jealousy for those doing better than us in an area where we ourselves want to thrive because, A,
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑天生会被那些在我们想要蓬勃发展的领域做得更好的人所吸引，甚至会产生嫉妒，因为，第一，

sentences.en: we are naturally comparative creatures and, B, comparison basically indicates desire, passion and what we want.
sentences.zh: 我们天生是喜欢比较的生物，第二，比较基本上表明了欲望、热情和我们想要的东西。

sentences.en: It's why, if you want to figure out what kind of life you want to have, you have to ask yourself, who am I jealous of?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，如果你想弄清楚你想过什么样的生活，你必须问自己，我嫉妒谁？

sentences.en: It's very revealing.
sentences.zh: 这非常有启发性。

sentences.en: And if the answer is, well, no one in the space that I'm in, you should probably be in a different space.
sentences.zh: 如果答案是，好吧，在我所在的领域里没有一个人，你可能应该换个领域。

sentences.en: And obviously I'm not condoning jealousy as a motivator.
sentences.zh: 显然我并不是在纵容把嫉妒当作动力。

sentences.en: I'm just saying that jealousy is a really, because it is such a deeply felt emotion, it's quite revealing of what you really want.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，因为嫉妒是一种如此深切的情感，它非常能说明你真正想要的是什么。

sentences.en: Also, you know, we so often learn and stay motivated through observation and modeling, but also through vicarious victory and celebration, you know,
sentences.zh: 另外，你知道的，我们经常通过观察和建模来学习和保持动力，同时也通过间接的胜利和庆祝，你知道的，

sentences.en: seeing what others achieve and feeling like we could do that ourselves.
sentences.zh: 看到别人取得了什么成就，并且觉得我们自己也能做到。

sentences.en: That's a huge part of aspirational psychology, having role models, having someone that you look up to.
sentences.zh: 这是渴望心理学的重要组成部分，拥有榜样，拥有一个你敬仰的人。

sentences.en: And if you don't have that, like you're missing out on a big part of how you stay motivated in a career, how you advance, how you seek more for yourself in this industry.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有这个，就像你错失了如何在职业生涯中保持动力、如何晋升、如何在这一行业为自己寻求更多的大好部分。

sentences.en: Let's talk about this dimension, though, which is having someone you admire in a space that you would never want to make money from doing.
sentences.zh: 不过，让我们来谈谈这个维度，那就是在你不愿意靠它赚钱的领域里，有一个你崇拜的人。

sentences.en: So what if your heroes are, I don't know, like Dallas Cowboy cheerleaders and, you know, you're never going to be a Dallas Cowboy cheerleader.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你的偶像，我不知道，比如达拉斯牛仔队拉拉队员，而且，你知道的，你永远不会成为达拉斯牛仔队拉拉队员。

sentences.en: Like what if your heroes are classically trained musicians and you've never picked up an instrument in your life?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你的偶像受过古典音乐训练，而你这辈子从来没拿过乐器，会怎么样？

sentences.en: What happens when you admire someone as a hobbyist of the thing that they have made a career as?
sentences.zh: 当你把某人当作你将其作为职业的事物的业余爱好者来崇拜时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Does that make sense?
sentences.zh: 这说得通吗？

sentences.en: Like you view it as a hobby, they view it as a career.
sentences.zh: 就像你把它当作一种爱好，而他们把它当作一种职业。

sentences.en: What happens then?
sentences.zh: 那会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, that's complicated, but I think I'm personally a firm believer that your job doesn't have to be the thing that you love most in the world.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这很复杂，但我个人坚信，你的工作不一定非得是你世界上最爱的事物。

sentences.en: So just because you have a hero in a certain field, like a musician or an actor or, I don't know, a tech guru,
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅因为你在某个领域有一个偶像，比如音乐家、演员，或者我不知道，科技界大牛，

sentences.en: like that doesn't mean that you need to suddenly quit your job and pursue what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你需要突然辞职去追求他们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: As long as you know that you're going to be okay in the future with not giving it a shot.
sentences.zh: 只要你知道，未来如果不去尝试一下，你也能过得很好。

sentences.en: If you are viewing this person as a personal hero and as someone that you aspire to be, are you going to regret not trying to do something similar?
sentences.zh: 如果你把这个人当作个人英雄和你想成为的人，你将来会后悔没有尝试做类似的事情吗？

sentences.en: Like that's a question you have to answer for yourself.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你必须自己回答的问题。

sentences.en: It is also completely okay to just admire them and feel motivated by their character from afar.
sentences.zh: 仅仅从远处崇拜他们并从他们的性格中获得动力，也是完全可以的。

sentences.en: As long as you are okay with that fact and you will be okay in the future with not giving your passion a shot professionally, that's totally your prerogative.
sentences.zh: 只要你接受这个事实，并且未来即使不在职业生涯中尝试追求你的激情也能过得很好，那完全是你的特权。

sentences.en: But again, if you genuinely cannot think of one person in your industry or in your profession that you think is cool, there is probably something better out there.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，如果你真的想不出你的行业或职业中有哪怕一个人是你觉得很酷的，那外面可能还有更好的工作。

sentences.en: Maybe your hero may not be an accountant.
sentences.zh: 也许你的偶像可能不是会计。

sentences.en: Maybe they will not be a professional pharmaciSt.
sentences.zh: 也许他们不会是职业药剂师。

sentences.en: But there should be at least one person, a colleague, a professor, someone else you're in college with, someone you think has a cool life,
sentences.zh: 但应该至少有一个人，一个同事，一个教授，一个和你一起上大学的人，一个你认为生活很酷的人，

sentences.en: a life that you can see yourself emulating.
sentences.zh: 一种你能想象自己去效仿的生活。

sentences.en: So we are down to our final sign, our final one.
sentences.zh: 所以我们迎来了最后一个迹象，我们的最后一个标志。

sentences.en: And it's one you may have already guessed.
sentences.zh: 这也是你可能已经猜到的一个。

sentences.en: It's burnout.
sentences.zh: 这就是职业倦怠。

sentences.en: It's sickness.
sentences.zh: 这就是生病。

sentences.en: It's feeling physically and mentally unwell.
sentences.zh: 这就是感觉身心不适。

sentences.en: If your body is giving you the signals, if your body is getting sicker easier, burnt out easier, irritated more, this career is probably not in alignment with who you are.
sentences.zh: 如果你的身体向你发出信号，如果你的身体更容易生病、更容易疲惫、更容易烦躁，这个职业可能与你是谁并不契合。

sentences.en: We often think that career decisions are purely intellectual and rational, but your body keeps the score.
sentences.zh: 我们经常认为职业决定纯粹是理智和理性的，但你的身体会记住一切。

sentences.en: I feel like everyone's heard that phrase.
sentences.zh: 我觉得每个人都听过这句话。

sentences.en: Your body keeps the score.
sentences.zh: 你的身体会记住一切。

sentences.en: And not just when it comes to trauma, chronic stomach aches, fatigue, headaches.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是在面对创伤、慢性胃痛、疲劳、头痛时。

sentences.en: Sunday scaries, you know, a really severe anxiety.
sentences.zh: 周日恐惧症，你知道的，非常严重的焦虑。

sentences.en: These are not normal.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是正常的。

sentences.en: These should not be dismissed.
sentences.zh: 这些不应该被忽视。

sentences.en: These are not just parts of being an adult.
sentences.zh: 这些不仅仅是成为成年人的一部分。

sentences.en: You also cannot just outthink them or outwork them or continue with this idea that it will get better.
sentences.zh: 你也不能仅仅靠过度思考或过度工作来克服它们，或者抱着它会好转的想法继续下去。

sentences.en: It will get better.
sentences.zh: 它会好转的。

sentences.en: It will get better.
sentences.zh: 它会好转的。

sentences.en: These symptoms are often rooted in very deep psychological occupational stress.
sentences.zh: 这些症状通常植根于非常深层的心理职业压力。

sentences.en: Your nervous system is probably in a prolonged state of low-level discomfort and distress.
sentences.zh: 你的神经系统可能处于长期轻度不适和痛苦的状态中。

sentences.en: And this is ricocheting into all these other areas of your body, into tension, into a suppressed immune system.
sentences.zh: 这正在反弹到你身体的所有其他部位，导致紧张，导致免疫系统受抑制。

sentences.en: Even if you're still, you know, clocking in every morning, even if you feel like you can get through it, if your body is telling you no, listen to it.
sentences.zh: 即使你仍然，你知道的，每天早上打卡上班，即使你觉得自己能挺过去，如果你的身体在对你说不，那就听从它。

sentences.en: And also, another reminder, you're not being dramatic.
sentences.zh: 还有，另一个提醒，你不是在小题大做。

sentences.en: Even if people have it tougher, even if people work harder than you, even if you feel like you don't deserve to be stressed,
sentences.zh: 即使别人的处境更艰难，即使别人比你更努力工作，即使你觉得自己不应该感到压力，

sentences.en: I'm going to tell you, that's actually not your choice.
sentences.zh: 我要告诉你，这其实由不得你选择。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, it's not your choice.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉，这由不得你选择。

sentences.en: Like, you can't think, you can't think in a way of like, I can escape this by telling myself that I don't deserve to feel this way.
sentences.zh: 就像，你不能这样想，你不能用“我可以通过告诉自己我不应该有这种感觉来逃避”这种方式去思考。

sentences.en: Like, your body is not something that you can control with your mind.
sentences.zh: 就像，你的身体不是你可以用你的思维来控制的东西。

sentences.en: Like, you can't just tell it to be well if it's in an environment that is making it sick.
sentences.zh: 就像，如果它身处一个使其生病的环境中，你不能只是告诉它要保持健康。

sentences.en: So, it's something you really need to pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是你需要真正关注的事情。

sentences.en: Scientific studies have shown us that occupational dissatisfaction takes a toll on your body.
sentences.zh: 科学研究表明，职业上的不满意会对你的身体造成损害。

sentences.en: For starters, one study found that you sleep less, you get sick more often, you're more likely to report chronic stress.
sentences.zh: 首先，一项研究发现，你的睡眠减少了，你生病的频率更高了，你更有可能报告慢性压力。

sentences.en: One of the most shocking studies on this was actually recent.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，最令人震惊的研究之一其实是最近才出来的。

sentences.en: And it analyzed data from over 6,000 participants in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth
sentences.zh: 它分析了来自全国青年纵向调查的6000多名参与者的数据，

sentences.en: and found that job-related dissatisfaction experienced in your 20s and 30s can lead to overall health issues just 10 to 20 years down the line.
sentences.zh: 发现你在20多岁和30多岁时经历的工作相关的不满意，可能会在短短10到20年后导致整体健康问题。

sentences.en: With the real cumulative effect of unhappiness in your job really starting to show up in our health around 40.
sentences.zh: 工作中不快乐的真正累积效应大约在我们40岁时开始在我们的健康状况中显现出来。

sentences.en: The researchers, they examined the participants' job satisfaction from 25 to 39 and then compared that with data around their health after they turned 40.
sentences.zh: 研究人员调查了参与者从25岁到39岁 Job 的工作满意度，然后将其与他们40岁之后健康状况的数据进行比较。

sentences.en: And what they discovered was that people who were unhappier in their jobs early in their careers were more prone to illnesses,
sentences.zh: 他们发现的是，在职业生涯早期对工作更不满意的人更容易生病，

sentences.en: particularly mental health problems, but also sleep problems and excessive worry and excessive stress.
sentences.zh: 特别是心理健康问题，还有睡眠问题以及过度担忧和过度压力。

sentences.en: And this was when they were controlling for all these other variables, including income, including education levels, including where someone lived.
sentences.zh: 这是在他们控制了所有这些其他变量的情况下，包括收入、教育水平以及某人居住的地方。

sentences.en: This isn't just about your happiness.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅关乎你的快乐。

sentences.en: This is about your health.
sentences.zh: 这关乎你的健康。

sentences.en: And that's something that we don't value enough until we don't have it.
sentences.zh: 而在我们失去它之前，我们对这一点的重视还远远不够。

sentences.en: Trust me, like then your entire perspective changes.
sentences.zh: 相信我，就像那样，你的整个视角都会改变。

sentences.en: This is also about having a life and having experiences that don't feel burdened by a job that you feel trapped by.
sentences.zh: 这也是关于拥有生活和体验，而不是被你感到被困住的工作所拖累。

sentences.en: I want to quickly play you guys this clip from my other podcast mantra, because I think I put it so well there, like I'm not even going to bother repeating myself.
sentences.zh: 我想快点放给你们听一下我的另一个播客节目《Mantra》里的这段音频，因为我觉得我在那里表达得太棒了，我甚至都懒得重复自己了。

sentences.en: I think I put it perfectly.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我表达得太完美了。

sentences.en: This is from my episode on I make rest a priority in my life.
sentences.zh: 这是来自我关于《我把休息作为生活中的首要任务》那一集的节目。

sentences.en: I think it really applies to this episode.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它真的很适用于这一集。

sentences.en: I'm going to play the clip right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就要播放这段音频。

sentences.en: There is nothing more valuable than just getting to sit with your experiences sometimes and just allowing yourself to have a freaking nap,
sentences.zh: 没有什么比有时候坐下来静静体会你的经历，并允许自己好好睡个午觉更有价值的了，

sentences.en: like to have a nap, to have some downtime, to take a day off.
sentences.zh: 比如睡个午觉，有一些闲暇时间，请假一天。

sentences.en: You know, at the end of your life, I know it sounds so cliche.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在你生命的尽头，我知道这听起来很陈词滥调。

sentences.en: Everyone says you're going to look back at your life and what are you going to remember?
sentences.zh: 每个人都说你会回首你的人生，你会记住什么？

sentences.en: Are you going to remember the times when you didn't take a day off, when you worked too hard, when you missed important milestones, important events?
sentences.zh: 你会记住那些你没有请假的日子，那些你工作太拼的日子，那些你错过重要里程碑、重要活动的日子吗？

sentences.en: Or are you going to remember the day that you played hooky and, you know, you went and got ice cream with your parents?
sentences.zh: 还是你会记住你旷工的那天，你知道的，你和父母一起去吃冰淇淋？

sentences.en: Or are you going to remember the days when you said,
sentences.zh: 或者你会记住那些你这样说的日子，

sentences.en: I'm not going to let this stress me out anymore and went to dinner with your friends,
sentences.zh: 我再也不会让这给我带来压力了，然后和你的朋友们去吃晚饭，

sentences.en: even though, you know, you didn't meet your deadline or even though you felt this like urge to keep working?
sentences.zh: 尽管你知道你没有赶上截止日期，或者尽管你感到了这种继续工作的冲动？

sentences.en: That's a clip from my full episode, which is available on my other podcast mantra titled, I make rest a priority in my life.
sentences.zh: 这是我完整单集节目中的一个片段，该节目可在我的另一个播客《Mantra》中收听，标题为《我把休息作为生活中的首要任务》。

sentences.en: And on that, we really talk about why work is more than just pushing yourself.
sentences.zh: 在节目中，我们真正讨论了为什么工作不仅仅是鞭策自己。

sentences.en: And it's more than just productivity.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是生产力。

sentences.en: In fact, life is more than just productivity.
sentences.zh: 事实上，生活不仅仅是生产力。

sentences.en: And I think that's a real great place to finish and a real final reminder.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个完美的结束点，也是一个真正的最终提醒。

sentences.en: If your entire life is dictated by a job you hate and by a career you don't see a future in,
sentences.zh: 如果你的整个生活都被一份你讨厌的工作和一个你看不到未来的职业所支配，

sentences.en: such that it drowns out all the other parts of your life and it has you ignoring small joys and it has you just like sick with worry and unable to do the fun things,
sentences.zh: 以至于它淹没了你生活中所有其他部分，让你忽略了小小的快乐，让你因忧虑而生病，无法做有趣的事情，

sentences.en: that's going to have an impact.
sentences.zh: 那将产生影响。

sentences.en: And the sooner that you can start searching for an alternative, start just questioning if there is something else out there you would enjoy more,
sentences.zh: 你越早开始寻找替代方案，越早开始质疑是否有其他你更喜欢的事物存在，

sentences.en: the better, like the more your future self is going to start thanking you sooner, like the better off you will be.
sentences.zh: 就越好，就像你未来的自己会越早开始感谢你一样，你的处境就会越好。

sentences.en: The time to change is now.
sentences.zh: 改变的时刻就是现在。

sentences.en: And that's at any age, by the way, whatever age you are, it's still now.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，任何年龄都是如此，无论你多大，现在都还来得及。

sentences.en: But speaking to all my 20-somethings, you know, starting again, going back, saying this degree isn't right for me, I don't want to do this anymore,
sentences.zh: 但是对所有20多岁的朋友们说，你知道的，重新开始，回头说这个学位不适合我，我不想再这样做了，

sentences.en: I'm going to choose to be a beginner, that is not shameful, that does not make me a failure.
sentences.zh: 我选择成为一个初学者，这并不可耻，这并不意味着我是个失败者。

sentences.en: I think that that is an incredible act of bravery.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种不可思议的勇敢行为。

sentences.en: Choosing to start again, choosing to acknowledge that this wasn't right, you didn't make a mistake, you just didn't have all the information yet, is so courageous.
sentences.zh: 选择重新开始，选择承认这并不合适，你没有犯错，你只是还没有掌握所有的信息，这是多么勇敢啊。

sentences.en: Like that makes you a major success in my eyes.
sentences.zh: 就像这在我眼里让你成为了一个巨大成功的人。

sentences.en: Like those are the kinds of people I really admire and the stories I really seek out.
sentences.zh: 就像这些才是我真正钦佩的人，也是我真正寻找的故事。

sentences.en: Like those are people who are not afraid to start over and who are not afraid of being a beginner
sentences.zh: 就像那些不害怕重新开始、不害怕成为初学者的人，

sentences.en: and saying I was wrong about what I wanted and now I'm just going to see and I'm going to explore.
sentences.zh: 并说我之前对自己想要什么弄错了，现在我只是要去看看，我要去探索。

sentences.en: You have so much time and that time will be more valuable when you spend it doing something aligned with what you care about.
sentences.zh: 你有那么多的时间，当你把这些时间花在做符合你所关心的事情上时，这些时间会更有价值。

sentences.en: And when you spend it doing something that really puts a fire in your belly or that gives you a sense of being
sentences.zh: 当你把时间花在做一些真正能点燃你内心激情的事情上，或者给你一种存在感，

sentences.en: or a mission or just a sense of accomplishment, whatever name you want to give it,
sentences.zh: 或者一种使命感，或者仅仅是一种成就感，不管你想给它起什么名字，

sentences.en: having a job and having a career that you feel proud to have is really great for your mental health, firstly.
sentences.zh: 首先，拥有一份让你感到自豪的工作和职业对你的心理健康真的很有好处。

sentences.en: It's also really great for your physical health and it's really great for the enjoyment that you want to get out of life.
sentences.zh: 它对你的身体健康也真的很有好处，对你想从生活中获得的乐趣也真的很有好处。

sentences.en: So I hope that this episode has provided you with some clarity and with some answers.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望这一集能为你提供一些清晰的思路和一些答案。

sentences.en: If you have made it this far, you guys know that if you make it to the end of the episode, you get a secret message from me that I invite you to leave a comment on.
sentences.zh: 如果你坚持听到了最后，你们就知道，如果听完整期节目，你就会听到我的一个秘密口令，我邀请你在评论区留言。

sentences.en: If you've made it this far, leave a comment down below.
sentences.zh: 如果你坚持听到了这里，请在下方留言。

sentences.zh: 你的第一份工作是什么？

sentences.zh: 我的第一份工作是在一家叫 Boost Juice 的店里做果昔。

sentences.zh: 如果你是澳大利亚人，你就会懂 Boost Juice 的定律。

sentences.zh: 不过说到职业，说到那些可能并不适合我们的职业，你的第一份工作是什么？

sentences.en: But anyways, I hope that this has, yeah, again, caused you to question, caused you to reflect, caused you just to think about it.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我希望这能——对，再次强调——引发你的质疑，引发你的反思，让你去思考这件事。

sentences.en: You don't have to make any choices now.
sentences.zh: 你现在不需要做出任何选择。

sentences.en: You don't have to go out and quit your job tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 你不需要明天就冲出去辞职。

sentences.en: This is just a nice way for you to consider what else is out there for you
sentences.zh: 这只是让你思考还有什么其他可能性的好方法

sentences.en: and maybe confirm some things you already know about a deeper dissatisfaction with the career you've chosen.
sentences.zh: 或许也能印证你早已察觉的一些事，比如对你所选职业的深层不满。

sentences.en: That doesn't make you a failure.
sentences.zh: 这并不代表你是个失败者。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean you've made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你犯了错。

sentences.en: It just means that now you have more information to make a better choice for yourself.
sentences.zh: 这只意味着你现在有了更多的信息，能为自己做出更好的选择。

sentences.en: So as we wrap up this episode, make sure that you give that full episode on Mantra a listen.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们结束本期节目之际，一定要去听听 Mantra 的那一整期节目。

sentences.zh: 我会在简介里留个链接。

sentences.zh: 确保在 Instagram 上关注我，账号是 thatpsychologypodcaSt。

sentences.zh: 如果你想分享反馈、问题、节目建议，我们一直在寻找。

sentences.zh: 我们一直在留意。

sentences.zh: 在那里给我发私信。

sentences.zh: 记得关注我们，这样你就能随时了解新节目何时上线，并给我们留个五星好评。

sentences.zh: 如果你觉得愿意的话，这真的能帮节目成长，而且，没错，能接触到像你们这样酷的新朋友。

sentences.en: But until next time, stay safe, be kind, be gentle with yourself, especially if you are dealing with some career dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，注意安全，保持善良，对自己温柔一点，尤其是当你正面临职业倦怠或不满时。

sentences.en: A lot of people are.
sentences.zh: 很多人都这样。

sentences.en: You are not alone.
sentences.zh: 你并不孤单。

sentences.en: And we will talk very, very soon.
sentences.zh: 我们很快就会再聊。

sentences.zh: 一张照片，一件衣服，一个来自难忘之地的微小纪念品。

sentences.en: In my new podcast, Charmed, with Sam Todd, we explore the memories, obsessions, and personal treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: 在我和萨姆·托德（Sam Todd）合作的新播客《Charmed》中，我们探索了构成我们一部分的记忆、执念和私人宝藏。
